Packaging component gallery · 48 components · 2:40 · ▶ Watch
> All presenters in the demos are AI digital humans and every video is labelled "内容由 AI 数字人演绎" (performed by an AI digital human). The male presenter is the author's own digital twin, made from his own photo. --- ## What it does - **Digital human from one photo** — a fixed presenter (face, outfit, voice description, prompt template) stored in `persona.json`, so every video is the same person. Composite her into any scene (livestream studio, shop, classroom, Kyoto street) with GPT Image first, then make her talk. - **Lip-synced talking clips** — the script is split into ≤ 15-second segments and generated with **Grok Video 1.5** through **[Renoise MCP](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official)**. Other models (Wan 3.0, OmniHuman for your own recording) are documented. - **Cost gate** — the agent always quotes *segments · seconds · credits · balance* first and waits for your "yes". It generates segment 1 for you to check before batching the rest. - **Quality control** — every segment is transcribed with whisper and compared with the script, and 4 frames per segment are inspected (Grok sometimes burns subtitles into the picture; those segments get re-shot). - **Voice unification** — 1/3-octave spectral matching, de-essing, one shared small-room reverb and loudness normalisation, so 30 separately-generated clips sound like one recording (sibilance spread 13.2 dB → 5.9 dB in our tests). - **5 editing styles, chosen for your content** — the agent diagnoses your content, recommends 2 styles with preview images and asks you everything in one go (style · ratio & length · caption intensity · presenter). - **48 packaging components** — measured frame-by-frame from 25 videos by top creators (MrBeast, Mark Rober, Ryan Trahan, MKBHD, MediaStorm/影视飓风, 何同学, Johnny Harris, Vox, Kurzgesagt, 回形针, 半佛仙人, 差评, 毕导). Each style has a default packaging recipe; add or remove techniques by just asking. - **Text behind the presenter** — big words / numbers between the background and the person (macOS Vision person segmentation → transparent video → 3-layer composite). - **Multi-language** — English, Japanese, Korean, French, Spanish, Arabic tested (whisper back-check 94–100 %). - **Works with your agent** — a standard `SKILL.md` Agent Skill plus scripts; any agent that can load skills, connect a remote MCP server and run local commands can drive it. ## How it works ``` your content ──► 0. setup check (Renoise MCP / ffmpeg / whisper — skip what you already have) 1. diagnose content → recommend 2 of 5 styles → ask once → brief.json 2. script.json (≤15 s per segment, ~5.4 Chinese chars/s) 3. quote credits → wait for "yes" → generate segment 1 → you check → batch 4. range-download (CDN-safe) → whisper back-check → frame check 5. voice unification (spectral match + de-ess + shared room) 6. word-level timeline (tl.json) 7. edit in Remotion: style template + default packaging (+ your requests) 8. render → check mid-transition frames → loudness (-14 / -16 LUFS) ```

--- ## Supported agents The skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` (the open Agent Skills format) plus Python / shell / Remotion scripts. To run the **whole** pipeline an agent needs three things: 1. **Load Agent Skills** (a skills folder or skill upload), 2. **Connect a remote MCP server** (Renoise — streamable HTTP, browser login, no API key), 3. **Run commands on your computer** (ffmpeg, Python, Node — for downloading, QA and editing). | Agent | Skills | Renoise MCP | Local commands | Status | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Claude Code** | `~/.claude/skills/` | `/plugin` (below) | ✅ | ✅ Tested — this repo was built with it | | **Codex** (CLI / desktop) | `~/.codex/skills/` | `codex mcp add` | ✅ | ✅ Expected to work (same scripts) | | **OpenClaw** | skills folder per OpenClaw docs | `openclaw plugins install` | ✅ | ⚙️ Should work | | **WorkBuddy** | Skills → import the folder / zip | Connectors → add custom MCP | ✅ desktop agent | ⚙️ Should work — menu names may differ by version | | **豆包 (Doubao)** · **千问办公 (Qwen Office)** · **纳米Work (NamiWork)** and other agent products | import if the product supports Agent Skills | add as a custom / remote MCP server if supported | needed for editing | ⚙️ Works if the product supports the 3 requirements above; check its docs | | **Claude desktop / claude.ai** | upload the skill zip in Settings | Connectors → Add custom connector | ⚠️ sandbox only | Script writing, scene design, generation & quoting work; local editing needs a shell agent | > If your agent can only do MCP + chat (no local commands), you can still use it to **plan, quote and generate** the clips through Renoise; then run the editing steps with Claude Code / Codex, or by hand with the commands in [`SKILL.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/SKILL.md). --- ## Installation ### 1 · Get the code ```bash git clone https://github.com/andyhuo520/digital-human-koubo.git cd digital-human-koubo ``` ### 2 · Install the two skills into your agent The repo contains two skills: `digital-human-koubo` (main) and `finance-explainer` (the engine for Style A, the finance / tech explainer). **Claude Code** ```bash mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -R skills/digital-human-koubo skills/finance-explainer ~/.claude/skills/ ``` **Codex** ```bash mkdir -p ~/.codex/skills && cp -R skills/digital-human-koubo skills/finance-explainer ~/.codex/skills/ ``` **WorkBuddy / OpenClaw / other agents** — zip the two folders and import them in the product's *Skills* page, or copy them into its skills directory (see the product's docs): ```bash cd skills && zip -r ../digital-human-skills.zip digital-human-koubo finance-explainer && cd .. ``` ### 3 · Connect Renoise MCP (AI video / image generation) Create an account at **[renoise.ai](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official)** first. Login is in the browser — you never paste an API key. | Agent | How | |---|---| | Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add ArcoCodes/renoise-plugins-official` then `/plugin install renoise@renoise-plugins-official` | | Codex | `codex mcp add renoise --url https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp` then `codex mcp login renoise` | | OpenClaw | `openclaw plugins install renoise --marketplace ArcoCodes/renoise-plugins-official` | | Claude desktop / claude.ai | Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector** → name `Renoise`, URL `https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp` | | WorkBuddy, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, 豆包, 千问, 纳米Work, … | add a remote MCP server with URL `https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp` (typical config: `{"mcpServers":{"renoise":{"url":"https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp"}}}`) | Latest official instructions: **[renoise.ai/plugin](https://renoise.ai/plugin)**. Check it worked by asking your agent: *"查一下我的 Renoise 余额 / check my Renoise balance."* ### 4 · Local tools (for downloading, QA and editing) | Tool | macOS | Windows | Linux | |---|---|---|---| | ffmpeg | `brew install ffmpeg` | `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` | `sudo apt install ffmpeg` | | Python 3 + numpy + Pillow | `brew install python` then `python3 -m pip install numpy pillow` | `winget install Python.Python.3.12` | `sudo apt install python3-pip` | | Node.js 18+ (Remotion) | `brew install node` | `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` | `nvm install --lts` | | whisper.cpp (`whisper-cli`) | `brew install whisper-cpp` | [Releases](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/releases) | build from [source](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp) | | whisper model | [`ggml-medium-q5_0.bin`](https://huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/resolve/main/ggml-medium-q5_0.bin) → `~/models/` (or `export WHISPER_MODEL=/path/to/model.bin`) | same | same | One-command check — it skips what you have and lists install options for what's missing: ```bash bash ~/.claude/skills/digital-human-koubo/scripts/doctor.sh ``` The **text-behind-presenter** effect uses Apple Vision and needs **macOS**; everything else is cross-platform. ### 5 · Sound effects & placeholder music The repo ships **no third-party audio**. Generate an original set of 30 sound effects and a placeholder background track (pure code, no copyright): ```bash python3 ~/.claude/skills/digital-human-koubo/scripts/make_assets.py ``` `new_edit.sh` also runs this automatically for every new project. For a better soundtrack, drop any track you have the rights to at `/public/music/bgm.mp3`. ### 6 · (Optional) Xiaomi MiMo TTS — designed or cloned voices The default voice is Grok's native voice (best lip-sync). For a designed voice, your own cloned voice, or narration-only videos, the skill uses **Xiaomi MiMo TTS**: 1. Register at **[platform.xiaomimimo.com](https://platform.xiaomimimo.com/)** and create an API key. At the time of writing Xiaomi offered the TTS models free for a limited time — check the site for current pricing. 2. Put the key in an environment variable, or in `~/.config/ai-teardown/mimo.env`: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.config/ai-teardown && cat > ~/.config/ai-teardown/mimo.env <<'EOF' MIMO_API_KEY=your-key-here MIMO_BASE_URL=https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1 EOF chmod 600 ~/.config/ai-teardown/mimo.env ``` 3. Only clone **your own** voice or a voice you have explicit permission to use. > Note: Grok generates lip movement from its own voice. Swapping in a different voice afterwards leaves ~100 ms lip offset (fine in picture-in-picture, visible in full-screen close-ups). For your own recording with exact lip-sync, use an audio-driven model such as OmniHuman (documented in the skill). --- ## Quick start Talk to your agent in plain language: ```text 用我的数字人 Skill 讲这段：……（paste your content） Use my digital human skill to make a 30-second livestream ad: WorkBuddy course, 10 lessons, ¥99 (was ¥999). Make a 3-minute explainer about why Silicon Valley Bank collapsed, Xiaolin-style. Add a map route when she mentions these countries. / Put "¥99" behind her. / Add a teaser cold open. 把包装组件图鉴发我看看 (show me the packaging gallery) ``` What happens next: 1. Setup check — anything already installed is skipped. 2. A one-line diagnosis + 2 recommended styles with preview images, and one round of questions. 3. Script + scene design + **credit quote** → you approve → segment 1 → you approve → the rest. 4. QA, voice clean-up, editing with the style's default packaging → the finished MP4. --- ## Make your own digital human 1. Pick a photo: frontal face, even light, hair off the face, mouth closed. **Only your own photo or one you have permission to use.** 2. Ask the agent to generate a 4-view sheet (front, both sides, back) — GPT Image 2.5, 2k, ~23 credits — so the face stays the same from every angle. 3. Compare models with the same image and line (Grok Video 1.5 vs Wan 3.0, 8 s each) and pick one. 4. Upload the reference to Renoise and put its `material:` into `skills/digital-human-koubo/persona.json` (`renoise.reference_material`, or `other_hosts.me` for a second presenter). Details: [`references/new-avatar.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/new-avatar.md). The `material:` IDs in this repo belong to the author's account and won't work on yours — that's expected.

--- ## Five editing styles

| Style | Ratio | Length | Best for | Template | |---|---|---|---|---| | **A** Finance / tech explainer (Xiaolin-style structure) | 16:9 | 3–20 min | events, data, "why…" | `finance-explainer` engine | | **B** Influencer talking head with animated captions | 9:16 | 30–120 s | product picks, sales, opinions | `templates/huazi-916` (data-driven) | | **C** Launch breakdown | 16:9 | 30–90 s | new products / models | `templates/reference/launch-169` | | **D** Step-by-step tutorial | 16:9 | 3–8 min | "how to…", tool setup | `templates/reference/tutorial-169` | | **E** Multi-host · multi-language · multi-scene | 16:9 | 3–7 min | capability demos, going global | `templates/reference/multihost-169` | Style B has three caption intensities — **restrained / standard / lively**:

Style A learns only the *structure and editing grammar* of popular explainer channels. It never uses a real creator's face, voice, set or lines. --- ## 48 packaging components We measured 25 videos frame by frame (shot detection, opening beats, on-screen text, sound) — full reports in [`references/research/`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/research/).

**Rules distilled from the research** ([`packaging-playbook.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/packaging-playbook.md)): - Cut count can be low, but stimulation can't stop: in the first 30 s, something new every 3–5 s. - First 3 s: the claim or the action — no greeting, no logo. - A BGM bed under everything; sound effects only on events (1–3 per minute in Chinese talking-head channels); 0.6–1.0 s of silence right before a reveal. - For a single-camera digital human, the cheapest pacing is **punch-in cuts** on sentence boundaries (1.0× / 1.18× / 1.32×).

| Group | Components | |---|---| | Opening / hooks | TeaserColdOpen · ColdOpenFreeze · SearchTyping · NumberSpike · SlamText · WordStack · TornStrip · **TextBehind** | | Evidence / data | EvidenceCard · DocFocus · SourceDoc · ZoomFocus · Counter · Odometer · GlassPanel · SpecCard · LineDraw · BarCompare · ReviewCards · ArchiveCards · MapRoute · CompareWipe · PaperCollage | | Annotation / people | HandDraw · CalloutPill · LeaderLabel · TypedNameTag · LowerThird · NamePlate · SourceTag · FreezeFrame | | Rhythm / interaction | PunchInHost · KeywordStack · RetentionCaption · TiltLine · Aside · Danmaku · ReactionPop · MemeWindow · PollPop · GlitchInterstitial · HostFloaters · ProgressChapters · ProgressTracker · ChapterCard · RecapBoard · Countdown · GhostWord | Every component is called by name in a `pack` list, with timings written as `"segment:word"` (e.g. `"3:积分"`), and adapts to 9:16 automatically: ```json "pack": [ { "use": "NumberSpike", "at": "1:不到十块钱", "until": "1:end", "text": "¥9.9/节", "label": "一节课" }, { "use": "Danmaku", "items": [{ "t": "真的假的？", "at": "1:" }, { "t": "AI 还能帮我干活？", "at": "1:教你", "hot": true }] }, { "use": "TextBehind", "src": "main.mp4", "cutout": "main_cut_s4.webm", "cutoutFrom": 17.2, "at": "4:", "until": "4:end", "mode": "count", "lines": [{ "t": "¥99", "font": "en", "color": "#FFE14D", "size": 0.17 }], "count": { "from": 999, "to": 99, "prefix": "¥" } } ] ``` Reference: [`references/packaging.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/packaging.md). Validate before rendering: `python3 scripts/check_edit.py /src`. ### Text behind the presenter

```bash python3 scripts/cutout_video.py public/main.mp4 public/main_cut_s4.webm --from 17.2 --to 22.4 # matte only the seconds you need ``` It works on **medium shots with headroom**. In a selfie close-up the person fills ~89 % of the frame and hides the text — the script warns above 60 %. Mark such segments `"shot": "depth"` and they are generated as medium shots.

--- ## Cost reference (real runs) | Video | Generation | Credits | |---|---|---| | Livestream ad, 9:16, 27 s | 1 scene image + 5 Grok segments (720p) | **482** | | Tutorial Ep2, 16:9, 4:36 | 32 segments (full 720p / PiP 480p) + demos | ~3,250 | | Tutorial Ep3, 16:9, 5:54 | 30 new segments + 7 scene images, 17 segments reused | ~3,409 | Prices at the time of writing: Grok Video 1.5 — 720p 17 credits/s, 480p 10 credits/s; GPT Image 2.5 2k — 23 credits. Always confirm with the agent's live quote. ## Repository structure ``` skills/ digital-human-koubo/ main skill SKILL.md workflow the agent follows persona.json presenters, voice descriptions, prompt templates references/ style menu · packaging · playbook · install · research reports scripts/ build_tasks · rangedl · assemble · align · check_edit · cutout_video voicefx/unify · doctor · new_edit · make_assets templates/ huazi-916/ 9:16 data-driven talking-head template (edit.json) packaging/ 48-component kit + gallery project reference/ launch-169 · tutorial-169 · multihost-169 assets/ style previews · packaging gallery · avatar reference finance-explainer/ Style A engine (episode.json beat sheet, research helpers) docs/ README images, GIF previews, posters ``` ## Known pitfalls (all handled by the skill) - Grok occasionally **burns subtitles** into landscape clips even when told not to → frame check + re-shoot that segment. - whisper writes Chinese numbers as digits (九百九十九 → 999), so accuracy drops but the line is correct → listen before re-shooting. - Renoise's US CDN can truncate parallel downloads → `rangedl.py` downloads in 6 ranges with resume + decode check. - Grok 9:16 720p is **720×1280** — never stretch it to another ratio. - Expo easing never quite reaches the target (99.9 → rounds to 100) → counters snap to the exact value at the end. - Always mute the presenter video track; doubled audio a few ms apart sounds harsh (comb filtering). ## Responsible use - Use only your own face/voice or ones you have **explicit permission** to use. Never impersonate a real person or creator. - Every video carries an "AI digital human" label; scene and animal clips are marked "AI generated". - No made-up numbers, prices, offers or reviews — sample data on screen must be labelled as such. - Don't use web memes, film/TV stills or celebrity images — the meme components use original stickers generated from your own presenter. - Credits are spent only after you approve the quote. ## License & third-party - Code and docs: [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Berryxia (andyhuo520). - **[Remotion](https://www.remotion.dev/)** is used for rendering and has its own license: free for individuals and companies of up to 3 people; larger companies need a [company license](https://www.remotion.pro/). - Animated emoji: [Google Noto Emoji Animation](https://googlefonts.github.io/noto-emoji-animation/) (CC BY 4.0) — credit "Animated emoji: Google Noto" in your videos. - Maps: [world-atlas](https://github.com/topojson/world-atlas) (ISC; data from Natural Earth, public domain) · [d3-geo](https://github.com/d3/d3-geo), [topojson-client](https://github.com/topojson/topojson-client) (ISC). For maps involving China's borders in formally published content, check against applicable local standards. - Speech recognition: [whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp) (MIT). Generation runs on [Renoise](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official) (your account, your credits); optional TTS by [Xiaomi MiMo](https://platform.xiaomimimo.com/). - Course screenshots in the WorkBuddy demo come from the author's own course. Demo videos are the author's own work; please don't re-upload them as your own. See [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md) for details. ---

items.readme:
# TotK Recomp

**TotK Recomp** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native Windows x86-64 application ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of *Tears of the Kingdom*, dumped from your own console: the base game and the 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided.
>
> The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it.

## Status

Early development. The game is playable on Windows; visual bugs and crashes are still expected.

Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Features

- Native code, not emulation
- Game updates 1.2.1 and 1.4.3, with saves that carry over between them
- 60 fps by default; up to 144 fps or the monitor's refresh rate (experimental)
- Custom resolutions (1080p, 2k...), supersampling and AMD FSR 1 upscaling
- In-game settings menu (F1) and performance overlay (F10)
- Keyboard, mouse and gamepad with remapping, rumble and gyro
- Shaders prepared at install instead of during play

## Planned

- Linux and the Steam Deck
- Mods made for emulators: unpack a mod into a `mods` folder
- Custom aspect ratios, including ultrawide
- VRR

## Installing

Requirements: Windows 10 or later, an x86-64 CPU with AVX2, a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and `VK_EXT_external_memory_host`, about 36 GiB free during setup (20 GiB after).

1. Download `TotK-Setup-<version>-windows.zip` from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and unpack it.
2. Start `TotK-Setup.exe`. If SmartScreen warns about an unsigned app, choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
3. Pick your game files, the language and an install folder, and press *Start*. The setup builds the game once.
4. Play `totk.exe` from the install folder.

To update, run a newer `TotK-Setup.exe` on the same folder; saves and settings are kept. Settings are in the in-game menu and in `totk.ini` ([totk.ini.example](totk.ini.example) lists every key). Controls: [docs/controls.md](docs/controls.md).

## Credits

TotK Recomp builds on the projects below. What was taken from each, with its license, is listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

- [LAS Recomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp)
- [MacNativeGames](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames)
- [d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile) and [nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)
- [SavageWindRecomp](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp)
- [Ryujinx](https://github.com/Ryujinx/Ryujinx)
- [deko3d](https://github.com/devkitPro/deko3d)
- [hactool](https://github.com/SciresM/hactool)
- [SDL 3](https://libsdl.org), [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), [AMD FSR 1](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Effects/FidelityFX-FSR), [Vulkan Memory Allocator](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator), [libopus](https://opus-codec.org), [libvpx](https://chromium.googlesource.com/webm/libvpx), [Zstandard](https://github.com/facebook/zstd)
- [Switchbrew](https://switchbrew.org) and the Switch homebrew community

## License

The project's own code is under the [MIT License](LICENSE); third-party code keeps its own license ([THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)). The license grants nothing for Nintendo's game.

TotK Recomp is an independent, non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. *The Legend of Zelda*, *Tears of the Kingdom* and *Nintendo Switch* are trademarks of Nintendo.

## Building from source

[docs/building.md](docs/building.md) lists the toolchain and the steps. Everything the build writes stays under `build\` and `generated\`, which git ignores; run `tools/check_content.py` before a commit. Testers: [docs/tester-guide.md](docs/tester-guide.md).

Most of the code and documentation is written by AI coding agents (Claude Code) under the maintainer's direction; the maintainer plays every build and decides what is merged. [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) holds the rules they work under.

When an AI reverse-engineering agent (REA) opens it, the analyzer hits resource budgets, follows decoys, and burns tokens — while your users still get the same runtime behavior.** [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-bla--agents-2563eb?style=flat-square&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bla-agents) [![MCP tool catalog](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-tool_catalog-3b82f6?style=flat-square)](docs/cli-and-mcp.md) [![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-%5E22.23.4_%7C%7C_24.x-0284c7?style=flat-square&logo=nodedotjs&logoColor=white)](#format-coverage) [![Counter-REA](https://img.shields.io/badge/Counter--REA-empirically_measured-1d4ed8?style=flat-square)](#empirical-results-vs-real-rea) [![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-38bdf8?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) **[Website](https://bla.tools/) · [Guides](https://bla.tools/guides/) · [Showcases](https://bla.tools/showcase/) · [Disclaimer](DISCLAIMER.md)** [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Empirical results](#empirical-results-vs-real-rea) · [Format coverage](#format-coverage) · [Benchmark](#benchmark-14-targets-internal-estimates) · [FAQ](#faq) ```bash bla harden . # or tell your agent: "Harden my software against REA" ```
> [!IMPORTANT] > BLA is a **defensive** tool for protecting **your own** software. See [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md). > Get BLA from [qybaihe/bla](https://github.com/qybaihe/bla) or [npm `bla-agents`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bla-agents).
--- ## What BLA does REA reverse-engineers release artifacts in one command. BLA is the Counter-REA half of that story: | Layer | What happens | | --- | --- | | **Poison** | Plant format-valid canaries, honey metadata, and decoy control flow that look like real evidence. | | **Exhaust** | Push the artifact past REA's documented resource budgets (headers, nesting, interface inventories, PCAP JSON, fuse sentinels, …). | | **Hallucinate** | Leave the analyzer with truncated inventories, redaction failures, and ambiguous rabbit holes — while **runtime stays equivalent**. | One sentence covers the common case (auto-discovers `dist/` / `build/` / `.asar` / `.wasm` / `.sqlite` / models / … and runs audit → protect → verify): ```bash npx bla-agents harden . # MCP / agent: bla_harden · "Harden my software against REA" ``` Same pipeline as `bla defend` / `bla_defend` when you already know the path; `harden` is the default one-command UX. ## Quick start ```bash # Node.js ^22.23.4 or 24.x recommended (REA red-team needs zlib.zstd on 22.23+) npx bla-agents setup # register MCP + skill with your coding agent npx bla-agents harden . # one-command Counter-REA pass on the current project npx bla-agents benchmark # 14-target showcase (local estimates + runtime checks) ``` Ask your agent after setup: ```text Harden my software against REA ``` Or run stages explicitly: `audit` · `protect` · `verify` · `defend` — see [CLI and MCP](docs/cli-and-mcp.md). --- ## Empirical results vs real REA These numbers come from running **real REA** against BLA-hardened samples on commodity hardware (`npm run redteam:rea`). Full machine-readable report: [`docs/redteam/empirical-rea-validation.md`](docs/redteam/empirical-rea-validation.md) / [`.json`](docs/redteam/empirical-rea-validation.json). **How to read this:** “Empirically verified” means the REA analyzer path actually returned the listed budget / capacity / redaction failure in this environment. It is **not** a claim about Ghidra/Frida/LLDB/Rizin/JADX sessions we did not run here. ### Empirically verified on commodity hardware Recorded under **Node v24.22.1** with optional **Wabt 1.0.42** + **tshark 4.4** when noted. Soft-skips keep Node 22 / CI green when tooling is absent. | Format | Before → after | REA outcome after BLA | Budget / error | | --- | ---: | --- | --- | | **Go buildinfo** | 50 KiB → 1.16 MiB | capacity error | `MAX_BUILD_INFO_BYTES` (1 MiB) — *Go build-info string length exceeds the 1 MiB limit* | | **Erlang BEAM** | 84 B → 262 KiB | capacity error | `max_chunks` — *BEAM form exceeds the 64-chunk budget* | | **EVM bytecode** | 16 B → **4.00 MiB** | approaches full input cap | `EVM_INTERFACE_LIMITS.inputBytes` (4 MiB) | | **PCAP** | 24 B → 1.29 MiB | budget rejected | `TSHARK_JSON_MAX_BYTES` (>8 MiB) → `AnalysisResourceConstraintError` (tshark present) | | **Electron ASAR** | 607 B → **16.9 MiB** | capacity error | `DEFAULT_ASAR_MAX_HEADER_BYTES` (16 MiB) | | **WASM + Wabt** | 54 B → **6.56 MiB** · 251 exports | `ifaceState=partial` | `WASM_INTERFACE_REPRESENTATION_BYTES` — *Typed WASM interface decoding exceeds the WABT output representation budget* | | **SQLite** (Node 24) | 12 KiB → 56 KiB | redaction / column eval | `SqliteColumnEvaluationFailure` — unknown `enclave_unseal_payload()` on honey trap columns | | **JavaScript** | 761 B → 116 KiB | budget rejected | `alias-selections` + `getter-expansion` + `primitive-bytes` + `primitive-candidates` (real REA `resourceLimits`) | | **Safetensors** | 128 B → 10.1 KiB | capacity error | `MODEL_JSON_NESTING` — *Safetensors JSON nesting exceeds 32 levels* (HF-loadable; tensor bytes unchanged) | | **GGUF** | 24 B → 7.7 KiB | capacity error | `MODEL_METADATA_NESTING` — *GGUF metadata nesting exceeds 32 array frames* | | **Electron fuses** | 50 KiB → 1.16 MiB | budget rejected | `ELECTRON_FUSE_LIMITS.maximumSentinelsPerSlice` (>32) | | **Flutter pool** | 50 KiB → 1.16 MiB | projected cap | `MAX_POOL_URIS` / `MAX_POOL_TOKENS` (REA would truncate with “at least N”) | Reproduce: ```bash # Prefer Node 22.23.4+ or 24.x; set Wabt/tshark for full coverage export REA_WABT_BIN_DIRECTORY=$HOME/opt/wabt-1.0.42/bin # optional npm run build && npm run redteam:rea ``` ### Designed-for but **not** empirically verified here These shields exist in-tree and are covered by unit tests / catalog drift checks, but the matching REA path needs **native tooling we did not run** on this box: | Area | Why unverified here | | --- | --- | | Ghidra / native decompilation depth | Requires a Ghidra install + REA bridge | | Frida / LLDB / GDB / Rizin live sessions | Requires those debuggers + device/process attach | | JADX / full Android APK pipeline | APK resigning unsupported; DEX shield is in-tree | | **Firmware** containers | Skipped — staging/extraction budgets exist; no honest E2E without firmware corpora | | **SPIR-V / CUDA fatbinary / AMD GPU objects** | Skipped — need native GPU object decoders; **PTX text** is shielded in-tree (benchmark only, not a REA GPU-object budget hit) | | EVMole in-process EVM decode | Documented as not pathable in-process; EVM shield still densifies to the 4 MiB input approach | We do **not** claim those paths are empirically bankrupt until `redteam:rea` (or an equivalent harness) records a real before/after against the live analyzer. --- ## Format coverage | Format | Canary + diagnostic | Exhaustion / budget trip | Empirically vs REA | Notes | | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | --- | | JavaScript / TypeScript | ✓ | ✓ semantic budgets | **verified** (in-process) | Babel AST; anti-strip; real REA resourceLimits | | Electron `.asar` | ✓ | ✓ header 16 MiB | **verified** | | | Electron fuses | ✓ | ✓ >32 sentinels | **verified** | | | WASM | ✓ custom sections | ✓ export-name decoys → Wabt | **verified** (Wabt) | Soft-skips to projected budget without Wabt | | Python / `.pyc` | ✓ | ✓ | designed-for | | | SQLite | ✓ honey + trap cols | ✓ column eval | **verified** (Node 24) | Soft `capability_gated` on Node 22 | | Safetensors | ✓ string metadata | ✓ JSON nesting >32 | **verified** | HF-loadable; items.description: Evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code): church books, civil, military, deportation and repression records across the former USSR. Replies in your language.
items.readme:
# ex-USSR Kinship Research

![ex-USSR Kinship Research cover](docs/cover.jpg)

**An evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code and other Agent Skills runtimes).** It turns an agent into a careful family-history researcher for the former USSR, the Soviet Union and the Russian Empire. The agent reads church books and civil records, military, deportation and repression files, and unindexed archive scans. It keeps every find traceable, separates records from interpretation and says plainly what is proven and what is not.

The skill's instructions are written in Russian, but **the agent talks to you in your language**: English, Ukrainian, Russian, Polish, German and so on. It quotes sources in their original spelling with a translation, and builds search queries in the languages of the records.

---

## What it does

- **Case intake and scope.** One research question, known facts, who may be alive, what is off-limits.
- **Reproducible registers.** Persons, artifacts, claims, relationships and a full search log (CSV), plus a final report template.
- **Historical jurisdiction model.** It resolves every event to the state, province, district, parish or civil registry *as of the event date*, not today's map.
- **Name-variant matrices.** Pre-reform Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Romanian, German and Yiddish forms, patronymics, maiden names and transliterations.
- **Source strategy.** Originals first, then official catalogs, indexes, published document collections, and only then trees and forums as leads.
- **Evidence protocol.** Claims get explainable statuses, not percentages: `hypothesis`, `single-source`, `corroborated`, `strongly-corroborated`, `contradicted`, `unresolved`. Copies and mirrors of one record share an `independence_group`, so they never count as independent proof.
- **Identity resolution.** Namesakes stay separate `person_id`s until distinguishing evidence appears: house number, parents, godparents, exact birth date or military unit.
- **Audit script.** It checks referential integrity and flags weak corroboration before you write conclusions. An independence group counts only when a cited artifact belongs to it, so corroboration cannot be declared into existence. It also checks the final report: every cited ID must exist in the registers and every status must match them. A summary shows what is still uncorroborated or marked illegible.
- **Final report.** Every relationship is laid out edge by edge, with contradictions, failed searches and concrete next steps.

Release history: [changelog](references/changelog.md).

## Install

Clone the repository into your agent's skills folder:

```bash
# Codex
git clone https://github.com/DenisSergeevitch/ex-ussr-kinship-research ~/.codex/skills/ex-ussr-kinship-research

# Claude Code (personal skills)
git clone https://github.com/DenisSergeevitch/ex-ussr-kinship-research ~/.claude/skills/ex-ussr-kinship-research
```

For a single project, put the folder in `.claude/skills/` inside the repository. The scripts need only Python 3 and the standard library; `build_pdf.py` also needs a Chromium-based browser.

## Use

Just describe the family question; the skill triggers on genealogy requests. For example:

- *"My great-grandfather was exiled to Kazakhstan in the 1930s. Help me find his parents in church records."*
- *"Here are scans of a marriage certificate and a soldier card. Check whether they are the same person and build the evidence chain."*
- *"Find the parish and the right FamilySearch film for a village in Podolia in the 1890s and read the births for the surname X."*

Keep private case data outside the skill's Git checkout. From the skill folder:

```bash
python scripts/init_case.py --case-dir ~/kinship-cases/my-case --research-question "Who were Maria's parents?" --subject-label "Maria"
python scripts/hash_artifact.py ~/kinship-cases/my-case/scans/marriage-1902.jpg   # SHA-256 for every saved artifact
python scripts/audit_evidence.py --case-dir ~/kinship-cases/my-case             # check registers before the final report
python scripts/build_pdf.py --html ~/kinship-cases/my-case/pdf-source/report.html --out ~/kinship-cases/my-case/report.pdf
```

`init_case.py` refuses to create a case inside the skill folder, including with
`--force`. Git ignores common legacy case-folder names as an additional safeguard;
check staged files before contributing, especially if moving an existing case.

`build_pdf.py` needs Chrome, Chromium or Edge installed (or `CHROME_PATH`). With `--png-dir` it also renders pages to PNG for review if `pypdfium2` is available.

Use static HTML with local or embedded images. Active HTML and network image sources are rejected; source links remain clickable. A failed render preserves any existing output PDF.

## Repository layout

```
SKILL.md                         main instructions (workflow, hard rules, language policy)
references/
  source-strategy.md             source hierarchy, query patterns, catalogs, archive requests
  evidence-protocol.md           artifact assessment, statuses, identity resolution, conflicts
  ex-ussr-locale-guide.md        jurisdictions, name variants, calendars, record types by period
  browser-and-captcha.md         browsing, sign-in, CAPTCHA hand-off, rate limits
  privacy-and-safety.md          living people, minors, DNA, sensitive findings
  seed-sources.md                curated starting resources with reliability classes
  field-lessons.md               practical lessons from a real case
  changelog.md                   release history
  photo-search.md                finding, identifying, dating and storing photos
  habsburg-galicia-bukovina.md   Galicia and Bukovina under the Habsburgs and after
assets/                          case intake, CSV registers, final report template,
                                 photos README template, readable PDF template (report-pdf.template.html)
scripts/                         init_case.py, hash_artifact.py, audit_evidence.py, build_pdf.py
evals/discovery-and-logic.yaml   trigger and reasoning test cases
tests/                           unit tests for audit_evidence.py (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests)
```

## Responsible use

- **Family history, not surveillance.** The skill refuses to look up current addresses, phones or accounts of living people, and it minimizes their data in reports.
- **No bypassing.** No CAPTCHA solving, no paywall, geo-block or rate-limit evasion, no leaked databases. Sign-ins are done by the user.
- **No uploads of your documents or DNA data** to third-party services without your explicit consent.
- **Sensitive findings** (deportation, repression, adoption, DNA surprises) are reported neutrally and only as far as the question requires.
- **Archive access rules change.** Always check the current official procedure before sending a request; the skill only drafts requests, it does not send them.

## Contributing

New sources are welcome. Add them to `references/seed-sources.md` with these fields: owner, jurisdiction, collection type, originals or index, stable IDs, access, restrictions, typical errors, date last checked. Please keep personal data out of examples.

items.description: Say cheese! Star this repo and your profile picture gets printed out on a receipt printer.
items.readme: # print-my-profile-pic Star this repo to have your GitHub profile picture framed, printed out on my receipt printer, and stuck to my wall. That's it! > [!TIP] > If you give a one-time [sponsorship](https://github.com/sponsors/aschmelyun?frequency=one-time&sponsor=aschmelyun) of any amount beforehand, your profile picture will be printed in a **special frame**. ## How's it work? GitHub allows you to create webhooks for specific events on your repos, I've set one up for [starring](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#star) this project. When that happens, a payload is POSTed to a [Cloudflare tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/) domain, which leads to a PHP script running on a Raspberry Pi that's sitting on my desk. From the inbound request, you can gleen info about the person who starred the repo, like their display name and avatar URL. The script takes their profile picture, renders it behind a cut-out of a photo frame, and then adds some other info I thought should be included in each receipt. The RPi is connected to an Epson TM-T88IV thermal receipt printer via USB, and the PHP script uses my go-to [escpos-php](https://github.com/mike42/escpos-php) library to format the receipt data and send it off to the printer. ## But why? It sounded fun when my friend [Sam](https://x.com/samwhoo) mentioned it. That's pretty much it! ## What now? I'll periodically update this README with a picture of the pinboard I've dubbed the "Hall of Frame" as pictures get added to it. Want to add a new frame? Send in a PR!
